1.explanation:
1. overflow-menu.config.js: the static Nunjucks variants need a new “light” variant that injects the `--light` modifier into the rendered HTML so the docs site can preview the light style.  
2. overflow-menu.js (core JS): the vanilla component should support a `light` option and apply the corresponding `prefix + '--overflow-menu--light'` CSS class to the trigger/menu elements, matching how TextInput’s light mode works.  
3. OverflowMenu.js (React): the React wrapper must accept a new `light` prop, add it to PropTypes and defaultProps, and include `classNames({ [prefix--overflow-menu--light]: light })` so the light modifier class is rendered when requested.  
4. OverflowMenu-story.js: the Storybook stories should expose a knob for the new `light` prop (or add a separate “light” story) so designers and engineers can preview and test the light menu variant in Storybook.
1.bug_scenario: The screenshot shows the default OverflowMenu placed on a grey container (background-color #f4f4f4). The grey icon and menu boundaries on the light‐grey background have poor contrast, so the user wants a “light” variant (e.g. a `--light` modifier) to invert or lighten the overflow menu’s trigger and panel styles when it appears on medium‐grey surfaces.
